name: Syncthing
tagline: Device-to-device sync with no server and no account
description: Continuous file synchronisation directly between your own devices. Folders stay identical on every machine you pair; data travels encrypted between them and is never stored on anyone else's computer.
backing: A community project supported by the non-profit Syncthing Foundation and donations

maturity.rationale: Over a decade old, with a famously dependable sync protocol and a 2.0 release in 2025. The mobile story is the weak point.

strengths: Nothing to host: your devices talk to each other directly, encrypted with keys only they hold
No storage limit beyond your own disks, and no subscription
Untrusted (encrypted) devices let you keep an off-site copy on hardware you do not fully control
weaknesses: It is sync, not a cloud drive: no web interface, no share links, no browser editing
Two devices must be online at the same time to sync, unless you keep an always-on machine in the mix
The official Android app was discontinued in 2024; the community Syncthing-Fork continues under new maintainers, and iOS depends on a paid third-party app
Conflicting edits surface as duplicate files that you resolve by hand

featureNotes.mobile-apps: Android through the community Syncthing-Fork; iOS only through a paid third-party app
featureNotes.e2ee: Only your paired devices ever hold the keys
